freeze.frozen_at_commit: PRE-IMPLEMENTATION (no streaming refactor exists yet at freeze time)
freeze.rule: Thresholds and sample sizes are PRE-REGISTERED. Any threshold added or edited AFTER a streaming measurement is taken INVALIDATES the corresponding claim (AC#8). The AC#3 Nix-retry de-risk run (crash-kill-mid-nar) is NOT a streaming measurement governed by this freeze; it is the pre-existing standing oracle, cited here as evidence, not tuned against these numbers.
freeze.no_float_decision_authority: No float is ever the decision authority. Every gate below decides on integers (ns, bytes) or exact rationals {num,den} compared by cross-multiplication. Floats appear ONLY in *_display fields as terminal, human-facing renderings. KNOWN TENSION (flagged honestly, not hidden): scripts/sizeaxis.py + scripts/scalefit.py currently compute the fitted RSS slope and its 95% CI in Python float. AC#5's gate (below) therefore carries an IMPLEMENTATION OBLIGATION: reduce the reported CI endpoints to an exact rational and decide by cross-multiplication; a gate that lets the raw float be the decision authority violates the owner no-float rule and must be treated as a defect.

units.nar: bytes UNCOMPRESSED RawNarV1 (NarSize); NEVER compressed FileSize
units.ratios: exact rational {num,den}; compare by cross-multiplication, never by dividing to a float

sample_sizes.rss_slope_grid_note: TASK-65 DEFAULT_SIZE_GRID_MIB; >=5 distinct sizes so the fit is not on 3 points. Driven by `just profile` / scripts/sizeaxis.py, model key size.fetcher_rss_hwm_bytes_ram.
sample_sizes.ttfb_fixture: the ~110 MiB `big` / s6 correlated NAR (Content-Length path)

wall_clock_prediction.claim: UNCHANGED. Streaming is NOT a throughput/latency win. Per TASK-64, ~70% of the peer-path per-byte cost is below our code (QUIC-over-UDP + bao) and cannot move; the removable buffer copy is ~0.7 ns/B. A 110 MiB peer fetch predicted ~0.549 s -> ~0.55 s.
wall_clock_prediction.so: A measured 'no wall-clock win' reads as CONFIRMATION of this prediction, not as a failure of the task. The task's value is time-to-first-byte overlap and fetcher RSS decouple, not MB/s.

ac1_ttfb.measured_at: the HTTP client (Nix / test client), NOT inside the daemon; inspection is not an oracle
ac1_ttfb.bite_rule: the buffering counterfactual MUST FAIL the pass_rule: revert TransportNarSource::resolve to collect-then-Full and its ttfb_ns * 4 > total_ns (predeclared buffering ratio >= 3/4, i.e. ttfb_ns * 4 >= total_ns * 3), because under buffering the client sees byte one only after the whole NAR is fetched+verified
ac1_ttfb.unbounded_channel_trap: streaming into an UNBOUNDED channel that flushes at the end MUST also fail pass_rule (its TTFB equals the buffering TTFB); the oracle must observe first-byte-at-client, so a flush-at-end producer cannot sneak a pass

ac2_ac7_backpressure_inflight.counter: a NEW fetcher-side in-flight-byte accounting counter around the in-flight buffer (NOT holder store residency, which is the wrong side per the TASK-65 trap note); high-water mark observed under a deliberately SLOW-reading client
ac2_ac7_backpressure_inflight.counter_placement_obligation: The counter MUST sit at the LOWEST point that holds bytes pending client consumption - below any adapter-internal (iroh-blobs / libp2p /nar/4) accumulation. A counter placed ABOVE an adapter that internally buffers the whole NAR reads ~1 chunk and passes trivially at both 8 and 128 MiB while real RSS blows up - a green-for-the-wrong-reason gate. The counter's placement is the load-bearing assumption; it must be proven, not asserted.
ac2_ac7_backpressure_inflight.max_inflight_fetch_bytes_ram_derivation: 4 * STREAM_CHUNK_BYTES (65536). A small bounded window, independent of NarSize.
ac2_ac7_backpressure_inflight.pass_rule: hwm_bytes <= 262144 at BOTH 8 MiB and 128 MiB NAR
ac2_ac7_backpressure_inflight.size_independence_rule: hwm(128MiB) / hwm(8MiB) <= 5/4 (near 1); the bound does not scale with NAR size
ac2_ac7_backpressure_inflight.bite_rule: TWO negative controls, both must FAIL: (1) a bounded-channel producer that still accumulates O(NarSize) ABOVE the counter - hwm scales with size, exceeds 262144 at 128 MiB; (2) a producer that buffers the whole NAR BELOW the counter - this proves the counter actually OBSERVES the buffer it claims to bound (a counter that stays ~0 while RSS blows up FAILS the placement obligation). If the counter is vacuous (never populated) the AC is not met.

ac7_cancellation.cancellation_deadline_ns_note: test-injected SHORT bound (2 s). In production the existing integer envelope bounds it: body_idle_timeout 10 s (10000000000 ns), total 60 s (60000000000 ns).
ac7_cancellation.pass_rule: after a trigger, the fetcher in-flight counter returns to 0 AND the peer connection is closed within cancellation_deadline_ns; every accounting permit (serve-side reservation via Admission Drop, and the new fetcher-side counter) is released
ac7_cancellation.bite_rule: a producer that keeps filling the buffer after the consumer is gone, or a permit that leaks past the deadline, FAILS

ac5_rss_slope.driver: `just profile` / scripts/sizeaxis.py over the 5-size grid, slope_ci95 from scalefit (Monte-Carlo-verified coverage)
ac5_rss_slope.before_buffering_slope_display: 1.0322 [0.9928 .. 1.0717] (TASK-65/72; ~1.0 B RAM per B NAR, the whole-NAR buffer)
ac5_rss_slope.pass_rule: THE GATE is: streaming PASSES iff the fetcher slope 95% CI-high < 1/2 (decisive decouple from the ~1.0 buffering slope). A weaker sanity note that the CI must also EXCLUDE 1 is subsumed by the 1/2 gate and is NOT a co-equal condition.
ac5_rss_slope.decision_representation: reduce the reported float CI-high to an exact rational h_num/h_den, ROUNDING OUTWARD (UP) so the rational is never looser than the float (outward rounding is the ONLY direction that cannot launder a fail into a pass); then require 2*h_num < h_den (below 1/2) by cross-multiplication. The rounding direction is FROZEN here so the implementer cannot pick it post-hoc and re-open the freeze. See freeze.no_float_decision_authority for the sizeaxis-float obligation.
ac5_rss_slope.bite_rule: a single-point RSS check is unfalsifiable (TASK-65 note); the gate MUST be the fitted slope over >=5 sizes. Revert-to-buffering: the slope CI includes or exceeds 1 and FAILS.

ac4_framing.correlated_path_expected_size_some: response carries Content-Length == the signed NarSize (uncompressed RawNarV1 bytes), NOT bytes.len() of a collected Vec
ac4_framing.teardown: peer stream torn down on HEAD and on client disconnect (bounded by ac7_cancellation)
ac4_framing.pass_rule: both framing shapes asserted at the HTTP client; both teardown conditions observed

a_a_noise.a_a_rule: two identical streaming runs of the TTFB measurement must agree within the A/A band: |ratio_a - ratio_a'| <= 1/20
a_a_noise.separation_rule: the streaming-vs-buffering TTFB separation (>= 3/4 - 1/4 = 1/2) must exceed 4 * a_a_band (4/20 = 1/5); 1/2 > 1/5 by construction, but the MEASURED separation must still exceed the MEASURED A/A spread, else the delta is noise

oracles_must_bite: Each threshold above names its BITE (the counterfactual that must fail). Per TESTING.md, a gate that cannot be made to fail by a plausible regression is not an oracle. The load-bearing bites: (1) revert-to-buffering fails AC#1 TTFB; (2) a size-scaling buffer fails AC#2 inflight; (3) a leaked permit fails AC#7; (4) a single-point / CI-includes-1 fit fails AC#5.
